1.explanation:
These files are responsible for deciding when to wrap AST nodes in parentheses, how to print JSDoc comments, and how to format call-expression arguments:

• src/language-js/needs-parens.js determines whether a given node requires parentheses around it. It currently doesn’t treat a JSDoc cast comment the same way it does Flow or TypeScript casts, so it drops the parens.

• src/language-js/printer-estree.js orchestrates the overall printing of JavaScript/TypeScript ESTree nodes, including inserting parentheses when needs-parens says so. It needs to be aware of JSDoc “@satisfies” comments.

• src/language-js/print/call-arguments.js prints the argument list for call expressions (and assignments via function calls). It prints the inner object literal without reinserting the original parentheses, so the cast comment ends up on a bare block.

• src/language-js/print/comment.js handles placement of leading comments. It must carry along the JSDoc cast and trigger the parenthesization logic so that those parentheses are preserved in the output.

2.explanation:
• src/language-js/utils/is-type-cast-comment.js is where Prettier recognizes JSDoc comments that should act as type casts (e.g. `@type`, `@flow`, `@ts-check`). It currently doesn’t include `@satisfies`, so our new tag slips through as a plain comment. Adding `satisfies` to its detection regex will mark it as a type‐cast comment.  

• src/language-js/needs-parens.js is responsible for deciding when to emit parentheses around expressions. Once `@satisfies` is treated as a type‐cast comment, this module will apply the existing “always parenthesize after a type‐cast comment” rule, preserving the user’s `(…)` and keeping IntelliSense alive.
